title: Vector-valued Fourier coefficient
statement: Let $\Omega$ be a finite nonempty set with probability mass function $\pi$, let $V$ be a real inner product space, and let $B$ be a finite Fourier basis on $\Omega$ indexed by a finite nonempty set $\iota$. For a function $f\colon\Omega^n\to V$ and a multi-index $a\colon\{0,\ldots,n-1\}\to\iota$, define its vector Fourier coefficient at $a$ to be the expectation, under the product distribution $\pi^n$, of the product basis function indexed by $a$ multiplied by $f$ as a vector.
hypotheses_covered: $\pi$ is a probability mass function on $\Omega$
$V$ is a real inner product space
The basis index set $\iota$ is finite and nonempty
The index set has decidable equality
$a$ is a multi-index with values in $\iota$
